  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which are
not listed on the agenda, but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no
action may be taken, the Commission and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items
needing response. Each speaker is limited to three (3) minutes.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous
meeting where the public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not
subject to public discussion at this meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final.
Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the
decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If
discussion is desired, an item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual
consideration. Commissioners may indicate a negative or abstaining vote on any individual item by so
declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent Calendar. Items excluded from the
 Youth Commission Regular Meeting Agenda  Page 3 of 3  May 7, 2026

Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the Consent Calendar. The
Commission first will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been submitted. Public
speakers shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this
meeting with no final action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under
Oral Communication.

Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment
shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described
above are on file in the office of the City Manager, and available upon request by emailing
KManisco@malibucity.org.

The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device
for the deaf (TDD), please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In
compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this
meeting, please contact Yolanda Bundy, Community Development Director, at (310) 456-2489, ext.
229. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to
ensure accessibility to this meeting. [28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title II].

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing
agenda was posted in accordance with the applicable legal requirements. Dated this 4th day of May 2026
at 1:00 p.m.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Youth Commission Goals 2026-27

  Recommended Action: 1) Review the Youth Commission goals for Fiscal Year
  2025-26; and 2) Approve Youth Commission goals for Fiscal Year 2026-27.

  Deputy Director Manisco presented the staff report.

  Commissioner Webb recommended coordinating teen social events, including film
  screenings and board game nights.

  Commissioner Kaplan suggested coordinating teen events with emphasis on
  localized content, including Pacific Coast Highway Safety for Teen Drivers.

  Commissioner Myers recommended a workshop on job readiness for high school
  students, and to modify the Youth Government Summit Series to different career
  fields.

  Commissioner G. Polatin suggested environmental sustainability programs,
  including park beautification days and beach clean-up days.

  Commissioner P. Polatin recommended hikes to encourage physical fitness and
  mental wellness.

  Commissioner K. Morra suggested mindfulness classes to improve mental
  wellness.

  Commissioner H. Morra supported goat yoga classes to improve mental wellness.

  Commissioner Magna recommended a variety of separate activities for middle
  school and high school students, as well as some combined activities.

  Commissioner Myers agreed with Commissioner Magna and supported a semi-
  consistent schedule for programs and events.

  Commissioner P. Polatin recommended expanding the list of special events at
  which Commissioners can volunteer to include the Poetry Summit, the Malibu
  Library Speakers Series, and other City community events.

CONSENSUS By Consensus, the Commission requested that staff update the proposed goals for
  the 2026-27 Fiscal Year and bring the item back to the May 7, 2026, Regular
  meeting under Old Business for final review and approval.

Subject:  Youth Government Summit Series

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file an update on career development and
resiliency from Sarah Flores, Emergency Services Coordinator.

DISCUSSION: For several years, the Commission has hosted a Youth Government
Summit Series (Series) featuring speakers from local government agencies and non-
profit organizations discussing their career paths and responsibilities.

On November 6, 2025, the Commission approved hosting the Series with three speakers
to discuss their careers in resilience, higher education, coastal preservation, or
City/County government.

Sarah Flores, Emergency Services Coordinator within the Public Safety Department for
the City of Malibu, is responsible for developing and maintaining emergency response
plans and ensuring the Emergency Operations Center remains in a state of readiness to
respond to large-scale disasters. Her role also includes coordinating with partner
agencies and organizing and delivering disaster preparedness training for City of Malibu
staff and volunteer groups. Ms. Flores will discuss her job responsibilities, emergency
management and coordination work, education, professional achievements, and offer
advice for those interested in pursuing a career in public safety and/or emergency
services.

Subject:  Youth Commission Goals 2026-27

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Review and approve the Youth Commission goals for
Fiscal Year 2026-27.

DISCUSSION: The Commission is asked to review and approve the goals for Fiscal
Year 2026-27.

At the April 16, 2026, Special meeting, the Commission provided feedback to staff on the
2025-26 Youth Commission Goals in collaboration with the priorities indicated on the
2026-27 Youth Commission applications.

The Commission is asked to review and approve the Proposed Fiscal year 2026-27
Youth Commission Goals which include a combination of coordinating teen programs,
opportunities for community service-learning at City special events, hosting in-kind
donation drives to benefit local nonprofit organizations, and providing input on local
government policies and projects.

Once approved by the Commission, the recommended goals may be taken to Council for
final approval.

ATTACHMENTS: Proposed Fiscal Year 2026-27 Youth Commission Goals

   City of Malibu
  MEMORANDUM

To:  Joseph Irvin, City Manager

From:  Harry Barovsky Memorial Youth Commission

Date:  May 7, 2026

Re:  PROPOSED Youth Commission Goals for Fiscal Year 2026-27

At its Regular meeting on May 7, 2026 the Youth Commission recommended the following goals be
included for FY 2026-27:
  1.  Coordinate four programs focused on creating connections and community, which may
  include: film screenings, game nights, live music, educational workshops for new drivers or
  job readiness, or mental health wellness.

  2.  Each Commissioner will volunteer at two City special events, which may include the
  following Community Services Department Events (Art and Poetry Events, Breakfast with
  Santa, Chumash Day Native American Powwow and Intertribal Gathering, Halloween Bu
  Bash Carnival, Malibu Library Speaker Series, Santa Paws, and/or Tiny Tot Olympics).

  3.  Coordinate two community service-learning opportunities that promote environmental
  sustainability, including a Beach Clean-Up Day and a Park Beautification Day. Each
  Commissioner will participate in a minimum of one environmental sustainability program.

  4.  Coordinate four donation-based programs that benefit non-profit organizations.

  5.  Host a Youth Commission Summit Series with representatives from local government
  agencies, non-profit organizations, or other Commission-approved career fields regarding
  their career paths and job responsibilities.

  6.  Review opportunities for teen outreach and communication to increase attendance and
  awareness at programs and events.

  7.  Review and provide feedback on City projects and programs.

  8.  Make oral reports as needed to the City Council on Commission activities.

  9.  Submit a mid-year written report to the City Council on Commission activity.
